facts.statement: The genus Kwangsisaurus was first described by Young in 1965.
Kwangsisaurus is an extinct basal pistosauroid found in Guangxi, southern China, dating to the Early or Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Kwangsisaurus is an extinct genus of a basal pistosauroid known from the Early or Middle Triassic (Olenekian or Anisian age) of Guangxi, southern China.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, Kwangsisaurus orientalis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Kwangsisaurus orientalis.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from the holotype specimen IVPP V2338, a fragmentary postcranial skeleton held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: Kwangsisaurus is known solely from the holotype IVPP V2338, a fragmentary postcranial skeleton housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton includes 20 back vertebrae, six front tail vertebrae, a damaged shoulder girdle, and the right forelimb.
facts.quote: The skeleton consists of 20 back vertebrae, six front-most tail vertebrae, badly persevered shoulder girdle, and the right forelimb.

facts.statement: The original describer, Yang, incorrectly oriented the specimen by mistaking the neck for a tail and the shoulder for a pelvis.
facts.quote: Yang misoriented the specimen, mistaking the neck for a tail and the shoulder for a pelvis.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from the Beisi Formation of the Loulou Group at Fupingtun, Dengilu, Wuming, Guangxi Province.
facts.quote: IVPP V2338 was collected at Fupingtun, Dengilu of Wuming, Guangxi Province, from the Beisi Formation of the Loulou Group.

facts.statement: Yang Zhongjian, also known as Chung-Chien Young, named the genus and its type species Kwangsisaurus orientalis in 1965.
facts.quote: Kwangsisaurus was first described and named by Yang Zhongjian, also known as Chung-Chien Young, in 1965 and the type species is Kwangsisaurus orientalis.

facts.statement: The generic name combines "Kwangsi," an old name for Guangxi where the fossil was found, and the Greek word "sauros" meaning lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Kwangsi, an alternative spelling of the former province Guangxi, where the holotype was found, and from Greek sauros, meaning "lizard", a common suffix for genus names of extinct reptile.

facts.statement: The specific name "orientalis" highlights the East Asian location of this species, whose relatives were previously known from Europe and the Middle East.
facts.quote: The specific name orientalis is Latin for "of the east", as an emphasis on the east-Asian occurrence of Kwangsisaurus whose relatives were known from Europe and the Middle East at the time of its discovery.

facts.statement: Kwangsisaurus belongs to the parent group Pistosauroidea.
Kwangsisaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: The age of the fossils is uncertain but falls within the Olenekian or Anisian stages of the late Early Triassic or early Middle Triassic.
rejected.quote: Its dating is uncertain, but falls within the Olenekian or Anisian stage of the late Early Triassic or early Middle Triassic.

rejected.statement: A second species, K. lusiensis, was removed from the genus and is now considered related to Lariosaurus.
rejected.quote: A second species, K. lusiensis, named by Young in 1978 based on IVPP RV 100 and collected at Luxi, Yunnan Province from the Falang Formation, was removed from the genus and is now considered to be related to Lariosaurus.
